text:
I use a toothbrush and toothpaste.

The office was quiet, save for the rhythmic clacking of keyboards and the low hum of the air conditioner. Arthur sat at his desk, trying to ignore the bright yellow feathered ball of chaos perched on his shoulder. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Arthur had made a grave error in judgment by bringing Barnaby, his African Grey parrot.

Barnaby was not just talkative; he was a spongy, feathered hard drive of corporate secrets.

"Good morning, Arthur!" chirped Barnaby, tilting his head.

"Shh, Barnaby," Arthur whispered, sweating profusely. "Remember the rules. No talking about the merger. No talking about the Q3 projections. No talking about anything that isn't 'cracker' or 'pretty bird.'"

Barnaby blinked. "Cracker. Pretty bird. *The CEO is embezzling funds through the Cayman Islands shell company.*"

Arthur’s pen snapped in his hand. He looked around frantically. His boss, Mr. Henderson, was walking down the aisle, holding a latte and a smile that didn't reach his eyes.

"Arthur!" Henderson called out. "How’s the new hire?"

Arthur stood up, knocking his chair over. "He’s... he’s very quiet! Very professional! He’s listening to me!"

Barnaby puffed out his chest. "Listening to you? *I heard you tell the board that the product launch is delayed because you lost the key to the server room.*"

The office went silent. Three heads turned toward Arthur.

"Bad bird!" Arthur hissed, grabbing a sticky note and trying to cover Barnaby’s beak.

"Bad bird!" Barnaby squawked, shaking his head free. "Bad bird! *Also, the coffee machine is rigged to explode if you use the wrong beans.*"

Mr. Henderson stopped walking. He lowered his latte. "Arthur, did you say the coffee machine is rigged?"

"No! It’s a metaphor!" Arthur yelled, his face turning the color of Barnaby’s feet. "He means... he means the coffee is strong! Like a bomb! Of flavor!"

Barnaby leaned in close to Henderson’s ear. "He’s lying. *Also, I know where the bodies are buried. Metaphorically. In the basement. With the broken printers.*"
